name: Lebanese Lentil Soup
description:
author: skipper-davies
Lebanese-Style Lentil Soup with Swiss Chard and Lemon

ingredients.name: Lemon juice, more
ingredients.originalText: ¼ cup of lemon juice, more to taste

instructions.text: Read the entire method first and measure the following ingredients before turning on the heat: 3 cups red lentils; 12 cups water; 1 large red onion, diced; 2 small Yukon gold potatoes, diced; 1 medium zucchini, diced; 4 cups Swiss chard, chopped; 1 bunch of cilantro, chopped; ¼ cup of lemon juice, more to taste; 1 teaspoon cumin. Keep ingredients marked optional separate until their step.

Prepare these ingredients before cooking: Red onion: large; diced; Yukon gold potatoes: small; diced; Zucchini: medium; diced; Swiss chard: chopped; Cilantro: chopped. Wash produce under running water before cutting. Use a cutting board and a sharp knife; keep raw meat and its utensils separate from ready-to-eat ingredients.
In a large pot, add lentils and water and place on medium heat to boil.
In a pan, sauté onions until pink, about 5 minutes. Stir frequently so the ingredients soften evenly without sticking or burning; reduce the heat if they darken too quickly.

Add chopped Swiss chard and sauté together until chard is wilted, 2-3 minutes. Stir frequently so the ingredients soften evenly without sticking or burning; reduce the heat if they darken too quickly.

After lentils have cooked about 8 minutes, add onion chard mixture, along with diced potatoes and zucchini to the boiling water. Mince means chop very finely; dice means cut into small, similarly sized pieces so they cook evenly.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Reduce heat to medium-low, cover the pot, and cook until the potatoes and lentils are completely cooked, about 12 minutes.
Stir and cook for about 5 minutes.
Add lemon juice and cumin before serving.

Turn off any burners or oven when cooking is finished. Follow the cooling or resting instruction above before cutting or serving. Serve the finished dish as directed; allow hot portions to cool enough to eat.
